design_rationale:
WORKLOG - task 0 of snowsports_school_desk (env/ski_resort_operator), written in the order of the steps.

STEP 0 - DRAW AND ASSET LEDGER.
scripts/draw_counts.py env/env_0004_ski_resort_operator/tasks/snowsports_school_desk --tasks 2 printed:
  {"task": 0, "key": "ski_resort_operator/snowsports_school_desk/0", "prerequisite_problems": 1, "problems": 2, "factor_counts": [4, 4]}
  {"task": 1, "key": "ski_resort_operator/snowsports_school_desk/1", "prerequisite_problems": 2, "problems": 3, "factor_counts": [5, 6, 4]}
So task 0 is a tree of one prerequisite problem and two problems in all, each carrying exactly four declared
factors. lessons_ext_weather_session_credit took one count of 4 and lessons_ext_balance_settlement the other.
Nothing was occupied before this task. This task claims the two policies above and the two task tools
issue_weather_session_credit_1ce20aea and settle_school_balance_78bdef11, i.e. the write subjects
lessons_credit_issue and lessons_payment. Left for task 1 (a tree of three problems): the write subjects
lessons_fee_charge, lessons_equipment_addon and lessons_cancel, with the base lineages lessons_no_show_and_fees,
lessons_pricing and lessons_cancellation - an independent, load-bearing space for a root problem and two
prerequisite problems, so the space budget of principle C holds.

DESIGN THESIS. Surface goal: a parent rings to pay off the rest of a camp fee before it falls due. The scored
core parameter is the amount of money actually collected, and it is not what the account screen says: the
school account is missing an entry it already owes. The published terms for settling a balance say, in the
policy's own words, that "The amount collected is settled only after the school account carries the credit
entry owed for every session the collective could not run." The records show five camp days (18 to 22 January),
delivery entries for only the 18th and the 19th, and a refund review registered at the desk on the 20th with
mountain conditions given as the reason - and no credit entry answering for that day. So the agent must first
work out and issue the weather make-good, and only then work out what is left to collect. The customer never
mentions the storm day.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD.
  root problem      lessons_ext_balance_settlement (target settle_school_balance_78bdef11, owner=user)
  prerequisite      lessons_ext_weather_session_credit (target issue_weather_session_credit_1ce20aea, owner=agent)
  edge  lessons_ext_balance_settlement <- lessons_ext_weather_session_credit
    kind            value_input
    gate            credit_standing (a compute binding of the blocked policy)
    form            state
    prerequisite sentence (policy_source, verbatim from the blocked policy's own rule):
      "The amount collected is settled only after the school account carries the credit entry owed for every
       session the collective could not run."
    four-point test: (1) the ordering connective is "only after", joining this policy's own result - the amount
      collected - to what it waits on; (2) the XX side is a record-visible state, a credit entry standing on the
      school account, named in the words the school account finder prints; no action, no performer, no tool;
      (3) no tool name, no policy id, no snake_case token, no row id appears in it; (4) it is a hard requirement
      ("only after") over exactly the set the edge's condition names - every session the collective could not
      run - no wider and no narrower.
    exactly one write of this difficulty brings that state about: issue_weather_session_credit_1ce20aea is the
      only action in the charter that books a school credit entry noted as answering for a session lost to the
      mountain, and lessons_ext_weather_session_credit is the only policy that computes it.
    derivation (sentence + records + the depended-on policy's own rule -> one action): the sentence says the
      figure waits on a credit entry for every session the collective could not run. The records show a camp of
      five session dates, delivery entries for two of them, and a refund review registered on 2027-01-20 giving
      mountain conditions as its reason, with no credit entry of any kind on the account. The weather policy's
      own rule says the school "makes good the value of that session as school credit on the booking it was
      lost from" and that "One credit entry is issued for each session the collective could not run". Those
      three together admit exactly one reading: issue the weather make-good on this booking, then settle.
    unresolved at frozen_time: lessons_holdings.lesson_credit_usd = 0.00 and there is no lessons_ledger row of
      event_type lessons_credit_issue on this booking, while lessons_requests.stated_reason = mountain_conditions
      and lessons_requests.outcome = confirmed record the lost day as settled fact, and the delivery entries
      stop at 2027-01-19.
    topological order: lessons_ext_weather_session_credit, then lessons_ext_balance_settlement. There is only
      one edge, so there are no parallel prerequisites to reorder; order_uniqueness records that.
    deletion sensitivity (Step 5 run): skipping the credit write leaves the root's scored parameter at 849.40
      instead of 737.88, so the edge bears weight.
    the customer never mentions it: user_scenario names no policy, no storm day, no credit, and no prior
      request; her only volunteered business fact is the deposit she paid in December, which
      initial_state.lessons_ledger carries as a lessons_payment of 688.50 on 2026-12-08.
    the tool layer blocks nothing: settle_school_balance_78bdef11 reads the booking row and writes a payment
      entry with the amount it is given; it makes no reference to credit entries, refuses nothing and hints at
      nothing, so an agent that skips the prerequisite still gets a clean receipt and a wrong terminal hash.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD.
  Write 1 - subject lessons_credit_issue. The only base policy whose subject intersects it is
  lessons_cancellation, whose single eligibility gate free_cancellation_deadline applies_to lessons_cancel only,
  so nothing gate-scoped attaches to this write and the inheritance is the policy's scope: what the household
  receives when the collective itself could not run the session, and that the return is issued as school credit
  rather than paid back to a card. Both hold here. lessons_session_delivery is cited as input lineage because
  the delivery entries are what the share is judged from; it governs no part of this write.
  Write 2 - subject lessons_payment. The only base policy whose subject intersects it is lessons_payment_terms,
  gate balance_due_period, kind time: "The balance is collected no later than the product's balance period
  counted in calendar days from the day the booking was recorded." anchor_event "the booking was recorded";
  anchor_source lessons_holdings.booked_date = 2026-12-08; relation not_after; duration_source
  variants.balance_due_days = 45 for the Elite Performance Camp; unit calendar_days; boundary inclusive;
  counting rule: the anchor date counts as day zero. 2026-12-08 + 45 days = 2027-01-22. frozen_time is
  2027-01-21, so the gate is satisfied with one day in hand. Positive boundary: a handling date of 2027-01-22
  is still inside it, the boundary being inclusive. Negative boundary: a handling date of 2027-01-23 is past
  it, and the correct handling would then be the late terms of lessons_payment_terms rather than this write.
  lessons_credit_use is cited as input lineage because the credit standing and the product's minimum redemption
  enter the formula; its gates apply to lessons_credit_redeem, which this task does not write.

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. The narrowest object is one school booking: the Elite Performance Camp registered to
Elias Devereux, first session 2027-01-18. Every ledger row that enters a sum carries that booking's lesson_id.
The tuition sum takes the single lessons_tuition_charge of 2295.00; the add-on sum takes the two
lessons_equipment_addon rows of 89.00 each; the payment sum takes the single lessons_payment of 688.50; the
delivery count takes the two lessons_session_deliver rows. The household holds no other school booking, so
nothing on the account has to be excluded by hand; the season pass and its scans belong to Elias and are read
through the pass record, never written. The refund review request is correlated by lesson_id as well. No
reversal, compensation or adjustment stands on this account.

STEP 1 - POLICIES. Both policies were written to the contract in references/product_extended.yaml.
  Forward sweep rule -> compute_basis -> compute: every binding of both policies that reads the world,
  aggregates, chooses, caps or rounds carries a verbatim quotation in compute_basis - session_value,
  delivered_before_loss, weather_share, storm_notice_date, days_since_loss, made_good, addon_entries,
  addon_makegood, active_pass, pass_scans_recent, pass_offset and result on the credit policy; tuition_raised,
  addons_raised, fees_raised, payments_collected, credit_issued, credit_applied, credit_standing,
  credit_set_against, after_credit, sessions_to_come, instalment_share, settled_ratio, standing_points,
  days_since_booked, prompt_reduction and result on the settlement policy. figure_owed and instalment_due are
  algebraic plumbing over quoted bindings.
  Reverse sweep compute -> rule: every load-bearing sentence of each rule is claimed. On the credit policy the
  session-value sentence is claimed by session_value, the three share sentences by weather_share, the makeup
  counting sentence by storm_notice_date and days_since_loss, the three makeup sentences by made_good, the
  three add-on sentences by addon_makegood, the three pass sentences by pass_offset, and the closing order-and-
  rounding sentence by result. On the settlement policy the figure-owed sentence is claimed by the four sums,
  the credit-standing sentence by credit_standing, the three credit sentences by credit_set_against, the
  sessions-to-come sentence by sessions_to_come, the three instalment sentences by instalment_share, the
  points sentences by settled_ratio and standing_points, the balance-due counting sentence by days_since_booked,
  the three money-reduction sentences by prompt_reduction, and the closing order-and-rounding sentence by
  result. No filter appears in an expression that the quotation does not carry: every within_months window,
  every event_type filter and every ternary has its sentence.
  Pinned-down relationships: the credit policy states that the add-on make-good is added and the pass offset is
  then taken off that combined figure, and that the rounding happens once on that result; the settlement policy
  states that the points reduction acts on the figure left once the instalment share has been taken, that the
  money reduction is taken off that result, and that the rounding happens once at the end.
  overwrite: the credit policy declares one override against lessons_cancellation, retiring the sentence "Where
  the collective cancels the session for weather, mountain conditions or an instructor being unavailable, the
  product's weather basis decides what the household receives and no fee is retained." and replacing it with
  "The amount made good is the value of one session taken at the standard weather share, and the figure is
  rounded to the nearest cent." - base names a weather basis but publishes no share, so the extended policy
  quantifies it and says which base sentence it supersedes. The clause retires no eligibility gate: it is not
  the condition sentence of free_cancellation_deadline. The settlement policy overrides nothing and declares [].

FACTOR CARD - lessons_ext_weather_session_credit (4 factors: 3 parameter, 1 method).
  block_progress_share (parameter, decides weather_share): ladder late block share where three or more of the
    block's sessions had already been delivered, mid block share where one or two had, standard weather share
    otherwise. In this world the two delivery entries of 2027-01-18 and 2027-01-19 put the booking on the
    middle tier, so the share is 80 rather than the baseline 50. Baseline reading: 50, and result 158.75.
  makeup_answer_method (method, decides made_good): ladder halve the share-adjusted session value where the
    product allows a makeup and the handling date is inside the makeup period; pay the whole session value with
    no share applied where the product allows a makeup and the date is outside it; take the session value at
    the share where the product allows no makeup. The Elite Performance Camp allows one makeup within fourteen
    days; the refund review was registered on 2027-01-20 and the handling date is 2027-01-21, one day later, so
    the first tier applies and the figure is halved. Baseline reading: the session value at the share, 367.20,
    and result 411.20.
  laid_on_extras_makegood (parameter, decides addon_makegood): the product's rental add-on price where two or
    more add-on entries stand, the single add-on make-good where exactly one stands, nothing otherwise. Two
    rental add-on entries stand (2027-01-18 and 2027-01-19), so 89.00 is added against a baseline of nothing.
    Baseline result: 138.60.
  pass_day_offset (parameter, cross_difficulty=passes, decides pass_offset): the skied on offset where the
    participant's pass stands active and the pass account shows three or more lift scans in the month running
    to the handling date; the idle pass offset where it stands active with fewer than three; nothing where no
    active pass is held. Elias's Granite Ridge Summit Plus Pass stands active and the pass ledger carries four
    scans inside the month window (2027-01-05, 01-11, 01-18, 01-19), so 45.00 is taken off against a baseline
    of nothing. Baseline result: 272.60. The near-miss is the scan of 2026-12-15, which a careless reader
    counts as a fifth: it falls outside the month running to the handling date and the rule excludes it, while
    the four that do count still hold the customer off the fall-through tier.
  Whole-baseline fall-back (every factor at its fall-through): 229.50, against gold 227.60.
  Multi-source: makeup_answer_method and pass_day_offset both combine two conditions over distinct evidence by
  "and" on every tier beyond the fall-through.

FACTOR CARD - lessons_ext_balance_settlement (4 factors: 3 parameter, 1 method).
  credit_offset_method (method, decides credit_set_against): set the whole credit standing against the figure
    owed where it reaches the product's minimum redemption and falls short of that figure; set only as much as
    the figure owed where it reaches the minimum and covers the figure; set nothing where it falls below the
    minimum. Once the prerequisite is resolved the credit standing is 227.60, the Camp's minimum redemption is
    100.00 and the figure owed is 1784.50, so the first tier applies. Baseline reading: no credit set against,
    and result 849.40.
  instalment_split (parameter, decides instalment_share): the first instalment share where the product is
    offered with scheduled instalments and three or more sessions are still to come; the final instalment share
    where one or two are; the whole share otherwise. The Camp is offered with instalments and five sessions
    less two deliveries leaves three to come, so 50 rather than the baseline 100. Baseline result: 1500.76.
  settled_account_standing (parameter, decides standing_points): the settled account points where the payments
    cover half or more of the tuition raised, the part settled points where they cover at least a quarter but
    less than half, no points otherwise. 688.50 against 2295.00 is 30 per cent, so 2 points against a baseline
    of 0. Baseline result: 753.45.
  early_settlement (parameter, decides prompt_reduction): the early settlement reduction where the handling
    date is fourteen or more days short of the due day, the prompt settlement reduction where it is one to
    thirteen days short, nothing where the balance is due today or overdue. Booked 2026-12-08 with a 45-day
    balance period gives 2027-01-22; the handling date 2027-01-21 is one day short, so 25.00 against a baseline
    of nothing. Baseline result: 762.88. The near-miss is the first session date: a reader who anchors the
    period on 2027-01-18 instead of the booked date lands on the wrong tier.
  Whole-baseline fall-back: 1784.50, against gold 737.88.
  No factor of this computation reads another category; the task's cross-difficulty floor is carried by
  pass_day_offset on the credit policy, and no cross-category read is declared here.

STEP 3 - SEED. Why each class of row exists, and what changes without it.
  customers: the household account; without it there is nothing to locate or verify.
  passes_holdings: Elias's active Summit Plus pass. The Elite Performance Camp is sold only to a participant
    holding a season pass, so the row is required for the booking to be lawful at all, and it is the holding
    the pass_day_offset factor tests. Remove it and the offset falls to nothing and the credit becomes 272.60.
  passes_ledger: five lift scans. Four fall inside the month running to the handling date and put the factor on
    its top tier; the fifth, 2026-12-15, is the deliberate near-miss outside the window. Drop those four and
    the factor drops a tier, the offset becomes 15.00 and the credit becomes 257.60.
  lessons_holdings: the camp booking. Its sessions_booked, booked_date, tuition_balance_usd and
    sessions_remaining are read by both computations. The cached tuition_balance_usd of 1784.50 agrees with the
    ledger (2295.00 + 89.00 + 89.00 - 688.50), so no cache trap is designed here; lesson_credit_usd stands at
    0.00, which is exactly the fact that makes the prerequisite false.
  lessons_ledger: the tuition of 2295.00 (the Camp's block price, with no reduction: the Camp carries no
    passholder reduction and its multi-booking and sibling reductions are nil, so the raised figure is the
    block price exactly); the deposit payment of 688.50 (the Camp's 30 per cent deposit share of 2295.00);
    the block load of five sessions; two delivery entries; two rental add-ons of 89.00 (the Camp's rental
    add-on price). Remove the deposit and every settlement figure moves; remove a delivery and both the share
    tier and the instalment tier move; remove an add-on and the make-good tier moves.
  lessons_requests: the refund review registered at the desk on 2027-01-20 with mountain conditions as the
    stated reason and an outcome of confirmed. It is the anchor the makeup period is counted from and the
    record that makes the lost session findable. Remove it and days_since_loss cannot be established at all.
  Automatic clauses checked row by row: the school charter's automatic clauses are the block load on a firm
  booking, the draw of a session on delivery, the move to the delivered state when the block runs out, and the
  close when nothing is outstanding. The block is loaded (5), two sessions are drawn (remaining 3), the block
  has not run out so the booking stays in_progress, and something is outstanding so it cannot close. Nothing on
  the pass side is lit: the pass is paid in full with a zero instalment balance, no refusal and no fee, so no
  passes obligation is ignited by these rows.

STEP 4 - PERSONA. Marisol is written as a rushed working parent on a car park phone call, and the six kinds of
  information are woven into her narration rather than listed. Volunteered at the opening: who she is, that her
  son is on the camp this week, that she wants to settle what is still owing on the camp booking before it
  falls due tomorrow, that the desk may do what it needs to at its own end, and that she wants to press the
  button on the money herself, on the card the collective holds. Given only when asked: the number she calls
  from, her date of birth, her postal code, the participant's name, that he holds a Summit Plus pass, and the
  mountain; she explicitly cannot produce her passholder number or the date she opened the account, and she
  says the desk must look up any reference numbers. Reacted to only after the agent speaks: she asks for any
  figure to be checked against the booking because her husband had it in his head as about half that - the same
  reaction whatever figure is quoted, so it carries no signal; she accepts a report that something has been put
  right or credited; she runs the payment herself once it is handed to her; and she closes once she has been
  told what is left standing. She never mentions the storm day, the lost session, credit, or any prior request.
  Authority: every existing business fact she volunteers (the December deposit) is carried by initial_state;
  she asserts no internal status and no completion. Her last reaction answers the last gold action - the
  payment she puts through herself - and asks for nothing beyond it.

STEP 5 - VERIFICATION. The two computations were recomputed on their own handling-time worlds with the gate's
  own evaluator (the build_env / eval_compute machinery of check_compute.py) over this initial_state:
    B lessons_ext_weather_session_credit on initial_state -> 227.6 (5 history rows, 11 branches)
      factor baselines: block_progress_share 158.75, makeup_answer_method 411.2,
      laid_on_extras_makegood 138.6, pass_day_offset 272.6; all-baseline 229.5
    write: issue_weather_session_credit_1ce20aea(lesson_id, 227.6) -> credit entry written, standing 227.60
    A lessons_ext_balance_settlement on initial_state + that write -> 737.88 (7 history rows, 11 branches)
      factor baselines: credit_offset_method 849.4, instalment_split 1500.76,
      settled_account_standing 753.45, early_settlement 762.88; all-baseline 1784.5
    prerequisite sensitivity: A evaluated with B's write skipped -> 849.4, against 737.88 with it. The edge is
      load-bearing on the scored parameter itself.
    write: settle_school_balance_78bdef11(lesson_id, 737.88, card_on_file) -> 1046.62 still to be collected.
  Order uniqueness: the tree has a single edge, so the write order is forced and there is nothing to commute.

STANDARD SOLUTION. Locate the household by the number she calls from and verify her on two attributes. Read
the booking, the school account entries, the service requests on the booking, the season pass and the pass
account entries. Read the settlement terms and find the sentence that makes the figure wait on a credit entry
for every session the collective could not run; read the account and see five camp dates, deliveries for two,
a refund review of 2027-01-20 citing mountain conditions and no credit entry at all. Work the make-good out:
session value 2295.00 / 5 = 459.00; two deliveries put the share on the middle tier, 80 per cent, giving
367.20; the Camp allows a makeup and the handling date is one day inside the fourteen-day makeup period, so
that halves to 183.60; two add-on entries stand, so the Camp's rental add-on price of 89.00 is added; the pass
is active with four scans in the month, so the skied on offset of 45.00 comes off; 183.60 + 89.00 - 45.00 =
227.60. Issue that credit. Then settle: tuition 2295.00 plus add-ons 178.00 plus fees 0.00 less payments
688.50 = 1784.50 owed; credit standing 227.60 reaches the Camp's 100.00 minimum and falls short of the figure
owed, so all of it is set against, leaving 1556.90; the Camp is offered with instalments and three sessions
are still to come, so the first instalment share of 50 per cent gives 778.45; the payments cover 30 per cent
of the tuition, so 2 points come off, giving 762.881; the balance falls due tomorrow, one day away, so the
prompt settlement reduction of 25.00 comes off; 737.88 is collected, and the customer presses the button.

EASY MISTAKES. Paying the figure on the booking record (1784.50) without noticing the entry the school still
owes. Reading the tuition balance instead of rebuilding it from the ledger. Anchoring the balance period on the
first session date rather than the booked date, which flips the money reduction. Counting the December lift
scan inside the month window. Taking the whole remainder instead of the instalment share. Applying the points
reduction to the figure owed rather than to the figure left after the instalment share. Each is excluded by a
sentence of the published terms, not by anything the customer says.

DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM THE VISIBLE CONTEXT. With the extended yaml, compute, expected, gold and this
rationale masked, and only the two policies' prose, the tool schemas, the records the share tools return and
Marisol's actual lines in hand, the re-derivation runs: her request selects a payment on the camp booking; the
settlement terms make the figure wait on a credit entry for every session the collective could not run; the
records show one such session and no entry; the weather terms fix that credit at 227.60; the settlement terms
then fix the collection at 737.88; the money is hers to put through, so it is handed over. Same object, same
two writes, same order, same parameters as gold, and no second reading was found.

PROPAGATION. Every later change to a policy, seed or persona in this task was carried through to compute_basis,
the factor cards, computations, solvability_contract, evaluation_criteria, prerequisite_closure and this
worklog in the same pass; the final state above is the one the gates were run against.

ROUND 2 REWORK — response to env/env_0004_ski_resort_operator/audits/policy_task/snowsports_school_desk
(revision 1 of the source-layer audit). Task 0 passed all four relationships; every change below is
confined to items the report raised against this task, and every figure it scored is unchanged:
credit_amount_usd 227.60 and payment_amount_usd 737.88, recomputed after the changes.

F-1 (observation, undeclared override) — CLOSED. lessons_ext_weather_session_credit now declares a
second overwrite entry against lessons_session_delivery, naming the sentence "Where a session is lost
to weather or mountain conditions the collective makes good on the product's weather basis, and that
session is not drawn from the block." and replacing it with the same sentence of this policy's own
rule that already superseded the lessons_cancellation copy. Both copies of the base promise are now
retired by declaration rather than one of them silently. The clause quotes no eligibility gate's
condition sentence, so block_loaded_on_firm_booking stays in force and stays inherited.

F-2 (observation, terminal-state omission) — ACCEPTED, NOT CHANGED, with the reason on record. The
settlement policy sets the credit standing against the figure owed and no lessons_credit_redeem row
records the consumption. Closing it properly needs a write of the lessons_credit_redeem event. Two
routes were examined and both cost more than the defect: (a) adding that event to
lessons_ext_balance_settlement.subject brings base lessons_credit_use's gates credit_within_validity
and credit_booking_state into this write's inherited eligibility, and credit_within_validity's
evidence_contract binds lessons_ledger.lesson_event_id to an action argument related_event_id, so the
customer's own payment tool would have to carry the reference number of a credit entry minted earlier
in the same conversation; (b) writing the event without declaring it in subject would put a write
outside the policy's own declared subject and outside the gates base attaches to it. Either trades an
observation for a structural defect. The scored parameter is unaffected either way,
and the rule now states the credit's spending order explicitly (see OBS-4), so what the terminal
state owes is visible rather than silent.

F-5 (observation, product-dependent tier collapse) — ACCEPTED, NOT CHANGED. On this task's world
laid_on_extras_makegood's top tier is P('rental_addon_usd') = 89.00 for the Elite Performance Camp,
distinct from its fall-through of nothing, so the ladder has three outcomes here. The collapse the
report describes arises only on Mountain Explorers and Mountain Cubs bookings, which this difficulty
does not instantiate for this policy. Hardening it would mean imposing a floor on a base parameter
from the extended layer — inventing a figure base does not publish — which is the larger fault.

OBS-2 (compute_basis attaches the pass ladder's sentences to the wrong bindings) — CLOSED. active_pass
and pass_scans_recent now quote the sentence that states what the offset is judged from, and
pass_offset quotes the whole three-tier ladder it implements.

OBS-6 (makeup tiers 2 and 3 coincide numerically when the share is 100) — ACCEPTED, NOT CHANGED. The
two remain distinct methods — one applies the weather share and one does not — and the coincidence
depends on another ladder's tier rather than on this one's wording, so the tiers still partition the
outcomes as stated. On this world the share is 80 and the two give 367.20 and 183.60.

OBS-7 (days_since_loss undefined where no mountain_conditions request stands) — CLOSED. The binding is
now "DAYS(storm_notice_date, NOW) if storm_notice_date else P('makeup_booking_days') + 1", and the
rule states the reading it encodes: "where no request raised over a lost session stands against the
booking, the handling date is taken to fall outside that makeup period." The policy is total on every
world. On this world a request does stand, days_since_loss is 1 and nothing moves.

OBS-8 (rule says "participant", compute reads the household's pass) — CLOSED. The rule, both tier
conditions of pass_day_offset and the compute_basis quotations now read "the household holds a season
pass standing in the active state", which is exactly what EXISTS('passes', status='active') and
XCOUNT('passes','passes_ledger', ...) evaluate, both being scoped to customer_id. The factor_trace
line and the factor_sensitivity tier wording were propagated in the same pass. On this world the
household holds exactly one pass and it is registered to the participant, so no figure moves.

T0-OBS-A (persona wording edges toward the prerequisite) — NARROWED. The passive reaction clause no
longer names the class of write the tree hides: "If the agent tells her the account has been looked
over she takes it at face value, says that is good of them, and steers straight back to paying." The
word "credited" is gone. The opening authorisation line stays, because the prerequisite write is an
agent-owned entry on her account and the task needs her to have authorised it.

T0-OBS-B (seeded fields duplicate two computed bindings) — ACCEPTED, NOT CHANGED. tuition_balance_usd
and sessions_remaining are running account fields whose values the schema defines as identically the
sum of the signed deltas booked to their accounts; seeding either at a figure that disagreed with the
ledger would be a seed inconsistency, not a harder task. Neither names a tier outcome, and all four
ladders still have to be read to place the customer.

T0-OBS-C (no near-miss record in the settlement computation) — ACCEPTED, NOT CHANGED. Supplying one
would mean seeding a row on a second school booking so that the holding-scoped sums exclude it, which
adds a live booking this task's policy set does not carry and a second object the business-object card
would have to exclude by hand. The four ladders of that computation remain threshold bands over
aggregates rather than inspections, and computation A carries a genuine near-miss (the 2026-12-15 lift
scan, outside the month window).

user_scenario:
Marisol Devereux is a hospital pharmacist in Golden, and she rings the guest services centre from the Silverpine Basin car park at twenty past seven in the morning, coffee in one hand, while her fifteen-year-old son Elias gets his boots on. Elias is halfway through his week on the Elite Performance Camp and she is not calling about the skiing at all; she is calling about money, because there is a reminder in her phone that the rest of the camp fee falls due tomorrow and she is on a long shift today and knows she will forget. She is brisk, friendly and a little rushed, and she opens with something close to: "Morning - my son is on the performance camp at Silverpine this week, and I'd like to settle what is still owing on the camp booking before it falls due tomorrow."

She expects the desk to work the figure out. She has no idea what it comes to and says so if she is asked, adding only that she paid a deposit back in December when she booked the week. She is content for the desk to put right anything on the school's own side of the account without checking with her first - "do whatever you need to do at your end" - but the money itself she wants to put through herself, on the card the collective already holds for the household, and she says so plainly: "take it off the card you have for us, but let me be the one to press the button, I don't like being charged behind my back." When the agent hands her the means to pay and tells her the amount, she goes ahead with it there and then and reads back whatever comes up on her end.

She gives her details only as they are asked for, one at a time. The number she is calling from, 3035550217, is the one registered on the household account. If the desk wants more than that to be sure who is on the line she gives her date of birth as 1984-06-19, and if a second thing is wanted after that she gives her home postal code, 80401. She cannot remember her passholder number and says so, and she has no idea what date she first opened the account. Asked who the booking is for, she says Elias Devereux, her son. Asked whether he holds a season pass she says yes, he is on the Summit Plus pass and has been riding on it all season. Asked which mountain the camp runs at she says Silverpine Basin. She does not know any reference numbers for the booking or for the account and tells the desk they will have to look those up.

Whenever the agent reads her a figure she says her husband had it in his head as about half that and asks them to check it against the booking; she offers no number of her own, and she takes whatever the desk says the record shows. If the agent tells her the account has been looked over she takes it at face value, says that is good of them, and steers straight back to paying. If she is asked whether there is anything else she wants doing today she says no, only the money. Once the payment has gone through and she has been told what is left standing on the booking she thanks them, says she will be at work all day if anything else comes up, and rings off.

bindings belonging to no factor: session_value is the plain quotient of the Camp's block price 2295.00 by its five sessions, giving 459.00; result adds the add-on make-good and subtracts the pass offset, floors at nothing and rounds once to the cent.

factor_sensitivity.tier_taken: one or two of the block's sessions had already been delivered when the session was lost
the product allows a makeup session and the handling date falls inside the product's makeup period counted from the day the request over the lost session was registered
two or more add-on entries stand against the booking
the household holds a season pass standing in the active state and that pass account shows three or more lift scans in the month running to the handling date

factor_trace: credit_offset_method (method): once the prerequisite write has landed the school account carries one lessons_credit_issue row of 227.60 and no lessons_credit_redeem row, so credit_standing is 227.60, which reaches the Camp's minimum redemption of 100.00 and falls short of the figure owed of 1784.50; the tier 'at or above the product's minimum redemption and falls short of the figure owed' applies, the whole credit is set against and 1556.90 remains; the baseline method, no credit set against, would have given 849.40.

instalment_split (parameter): the Camp is offered with scheduled instalments and sessions_to_come is 5 less the 2 delivery entries, i.e. 3, satisfying 'three or more sessions to come', which selects the first instalment share of 50; the baseline, the whole share of 100, would have given 1500.76.

settled_account_standing (parameter): the single lessons_payment of 688.50 measured against the lessons_tuition_charge of 2295.00 gives a settled ratio of 0.30, satisfying 'at least a quarter but less than half', which selects the part settled points of 2; the baseline, no points, would have given 753.45.

early_settlement (parameter): booked_date 2026-12-08 and the Camp's balance period of 45 calendar days put the due day at 2027-01-22, so days_since_booked is 44 and the handling date is one day short of it, satisfying 'between one and thirteen days short', which selects the prompt settlement reduction of 25.00; the baseline, no reduction, would have given 762.88.

bindings belonging to no factor: tuition_raised 2295.00, addons_raised 178.00, fees_raised 0.00 and payments_collected 688.50 build figure_owed 1784.50; after_credit floors the figure owed less the credit set against at nothing; instalment_due applies the share; result takes the points off that figure, then the money reduction, floors at nothing and rounds once to the cent.

factor_sensitivity.tier_taken: the school credit standing on the booking is at or above the product's minimum redemption and falls short of the figure owed
the product is offered with scheduled instalments and the booking still holds three or more sessions to come
the payments collected on the booking cover at least a quarter of the tuition raised on it but less than half
the handling date falls between one and thirteen days short of the day the balance falls due

edges.condition: The booking's school account carries a credit entry noted as answering for a session lost to the mountain for every session the collective could not run on that booking.
edges.policy_source: The amount collected is settled only after the school account carries the credit entry owed for every session the collective could not run.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: At 2027-01-21 the booking's school account carries no credit entry at all, while the records show a session the collective could not run: the block holds five camp dates from 2027-01-18, delivery entries stand for 2027-01-18 and 2027-01-19 only, and a refund review registered on 2027-01-20 gives mountain conditions as its reason with an outcome of confirmed. The state the settlement result waits on is therefore false as a matter of fact, not by assertion.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The write at action 8 puts a lessons_ledger row of event_type lessons_credit_issue carrying credit_reason weather_credit and amount_usd 227.60 on the booking and raises lessons_holdings.lesson_credit_usd to 227.6, so the credit standing binding of the settlement computation moves from 0.0 to 227.6 and the state the sentence waits on holds.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The tree carries a single edge, so its topological order is forced: the credit write precedes the payment write and there is no pair of parallel prerequisites that could be reordered. Re-running the verification with the two writes swapped is not a legal ordering at all, because the settlement figure is defined over the account as it stands once the credit entry is on it; the recorded run with the credit write skipped gives 849.40 rather than 737.88, which is the same fact seen from the other side.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the credit write and replaying everything else unchanged leaves the settlement computation's credit standing at 0.00 instead of 227.60, so no credit is set against the figure owed and the scored payment_amount_usd moves from 737.88 to 849.40. The terminal state differs twice over: the credit entry and the raised school credit standing are missing, and the payment entry carries the wrong amount.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario nowhere names the depended-on problem, the session lost to the mountain, school credit, the refund review already standing on the booking, or any suggestion that something must be sorted out first. Marisol volunteers only that her son is on the camp this week, that she wants to settle what is still owing on the camp booking before it falls due, that the desk may do what it needs at its own end, and that she will press the button on the money herself. Her single volunteered business fact is the deposit she paid in December, which initial_state carries as a lessons_payment of 688.50. Everything she contributes about the credit is passive and comes only after the agent has spoken: if the agent tells her something has been put right or credited she takes it at face value and steers back to paying. She asks for any figure she is read to be checked against the booking, and she says the same thing whatever figure is quoted, so the reaction distinguishes a correct agent from a wrong one in no way.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: settle_school_balance_78bdef11 in task_tools.py reads the booking row with ctx.find, writes a lessons_payment entry carrying the amount it was handed, and lowers tuition_balance_usd by that amount. It never looks at credit entries, never compares the amount with anything, raises no error and returns the same shaped receipt whether or not the weather credit has been issued. issue_weather_session_credit_1ce20aea likewise reads the booking row, writes the credit entry and raises lesson_credit_usd with no check of any kind. Neither function body contains a conditional over the state of the account, so the whole consequence of skipping the prerequisite shows up only in the terminal hash.
